title: Dataverse: create agent users with Microsoft Entra agent identity
summary: Hold: the guidance on logging agent reads omits Microsoft's production-environment and licensing restrictions, which administrators need before planning audit coverage. The roadmap facts and cited administration paths and API references are supported; smaller corrections concern the governance inventory and surrounding Entra and Copilot Studio qualifications.

claims.claim: Dataverse agent users have Microsoft Entra agent identities and are added to an environment for data access.
claims.quote: These users have agent identities in Microsoft Entra Agent ID and are added into the Dataverse environment to get data access.

claims.claim: An agent needing Dataverse data requires an Entra agent user associated with its agent identity.
claims.quote: For agents that require data access to a Dataverse environment, an Entra agent user must be created and associated with the agent identity

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Read and export audit coverage is presented as needing an extra activity-logging setting without its production-environment and licensing restrictions.
claims.quote:
The option to turn on activity logging is only visible when the minimum MicrosoftOffice licensing requirements are met.
User access or activity logging is sent to Purview for production environments only.
claims.fix: Replace the unqualified read-coverage guidance with: 'Microsoft points to Dataverse and model-driven apps activity logging for retrieve and export operations. This requires qualifying Office licensing and sends user activity to Purview only for production environments; do not assume it supplies read coverage for a nonproduction preview pilot.' Link https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/activity-logging-auditing/activity-logs-overview for the licensing review, Purview permissions and additional configuration prerequisites.
